machine.shared: A development machine, with other work running at times; the A/B runs are alternated for that reason

build.tls: OpenSSL 3.6.5 (bundled, static: linux-ext-libs 1.28); mbedTLS not built on this machine
build.note: CONFIG_DEBUG_TRACK_MEMORY is on (the .config of this machine): every allocation is tracked. A build without it does less work per allocation; that build was not measured here.

method.ab: Written on 2026-10-29, before the tag. 7.29.3 is the C code of main at ed0b524cb (YUNETA_VERSION 7.29.3; the release edits not yet committed touch no .c file), measured against 7.29.2, the last release with a study. The C changes of 7.29.3: build_path() of gobj-c (it returns NULL and logs when the path does not fit; every path of timeranger2 is assembled with it), the date reader of gobj-c (helpers.c), the ids of the lists of a treedb (list_id_yuno of tr_treedb), archive_purged_files() of timeranger2, rotatory_remove_old_files(), the Modbus and M-Bus masters, the agent, the controlcenter, archive_keeper and the cloners. Of the library objects, only helpers.c, rotatory.c, timeranger2.c and tr_treedb.c have other machine code; root-linux, yev_loop and ytls are the same. Measured: the same 47 figures as 7.29.2 -- timeranger2, treedb, C_TREEDB, the rotatory, the inter-yuno events, the TCP and TLS echoes and the BFF logins; the raw event loop and MQTT run none of the changed code and are only in the tag-time figures. The 7.29.2 side is a git worktree of the tag, its kernel libraries, the test module and the benchmarks built against the same .config, compiler and outputs_ext (linux-ext-libs 1.28 in both). The two binaries of each benchmark run in rotation, the order turned every round, a sync and a 3 s pause before each run (1 s for the three ctest binaries): 8 rounds, none left out (one run of the tm query on the 7.29.2 side took 37 ms instead of 13; it stays in, and the figure is noise). Mean +- standard deviation (median), t = the change over its standard error; |t| < 3 is noise. The BFF figure is the mean of the Msg/sec samples of a run, the first one (the warm-up) left out, on both sides. The one figure slower outside its noise (the appends with a live reader) was measured again: 7.29.2 and 7.29.3 alternated for 10 rounds, then a rotation of five builds for 10 rounds -- 7.29.2, 7.29.3, and the 7.29.3 benchmark object relinked with all the libraries of 7.29.2, or with only its gobj-c or only its timeranger2 (the two libraries whose code changed).
method.tag_run: The absolute figures of 7.29.3 are its side of the A/B run (its C code, ed0b524cb), measured on 2026-10-29 on the machine of the earlier reports; the raw event loop, the event loop with an append and MQTT, which the A/B does not run, were run at tag time on the same build: 5 rounds, a sync and a 3 s pause before each run. The per-second benchmarks drop their first and last second. The binary sizes are those of the yunos, the agent and perf_yev_ping_pong built from the main tree with the same .config.

story.title: Yuneta 7.29.3: a review round of fixes and a Modbus master that answers, at the same speed
story.lead: 7.29.3 is the fixes of a review round and a Modbus master that answers every request: build_path() refuses a path that does not fit, the date reader reads four more forms, the ids of the lists of a treedb, the archive of retention. Against 7.29.2, the last release with a study, 46 of 47 figures stay inside their noise; the appends with a live reader measured 3.7% fewer, on code that did not change, and inside their noise when measured again.

hero.text: prices: no figure got slower because of a change. The binaries grow 0 to 4 KB.

tiles: treedb: update a node and save it
story.ab_sub: Each benchmark built from the tree of each release (7.29.2 and 7.29.3), the binaries run in rotation: 8 rounds. A change inside its whisker is noise. Everything is on one axis: the change of the time an operation takes.
story.prices_sub: What got slower, how much, in which release, and what it buys.
story.no_prices: None. One figure measured slower outside its noise: the appends with a live reader, -3.73% (t = -4.7). It runs no code that changed: the append path has the same machine code, build_path() is called 82 times in a run of 360,000 appends and the date reader never, and the functions of the binary moved. Measured again it stays inside its noise in a plain alternation, and the 7.29.3 binary relinked with the libraries of 7.29.2 measures as 7.29.2: placement, not code.
story.abs_sub: Absolute figures of the 7.29.3 build (its C code: ed0b524cb), measured on 2026-10-29, before the tag, on the laptop above, as its side of the A/B run (the event loop and MQTT at tag time, 5 rounds): one process, one core for the event loop. Mean of the rounds.

ab.label: Appends per second
ab.meaning: How many records one yuno can store per second in a key-indexed topic.
ab.method: Each release built from its own tree (a git worktree of the tag 7.29.2 and the tree of 7.29.3, same .config, compiler and linux-ext-libs), the binaries run in rotation, the order turned each round, a sync and a 3 s pause (1 s for the three ctest binaries) before each run: 8 rounds.
ab.reason: Inside its noise in the A/B (t = -2.6), and the same placement as the appends with a live reader (the same binary): the append path (tranger2_append_record(), append_content(), the in-memory realtime lists) has the same machine code in both releases: of timeranger2.c only purge_key_files() changed (archive_purged_files() is inlined in it), and of helpers.c only build_path() (+52 instructions), the date reader and two functions no append runs. In a run of the benchmark (360,000 appends) build_path() is called 82 times, at the opens, and the date reader never; the object of the benchmark itself is identical. 3,003 of the 3,237 functions of the binary moved, most by 1,536 or 64 bytes; 21 changed their 64-byte alignment, none of them on the append path. Measured again: -0.74% (t = -1.4) with 7.29.2 and 7.29.3 alternated, 10 rounds, and -0.89% (t = -1.3) in the rotation of five builds; relinked with all the libraries of 7.29.2, +0.20%; with only its gobj-c, +0.19%; with only its timeranger2, -1.55%.

ab.label: Appends per second, with a live reader

ab.method: Each release built from its own tree (a git worktree of the tag 7.29.2 and the tree of 7.29.3, same .config, compiler and linux-ext-libs), the binaries run in rotation, the order turned each round, a sync and a 3 s pause (1 s for the three ctest binaries) before each run: 8 rounds.
ab.reason: Placement, not code: the append path (tranger2_append_record(), append_content(), the in-memory realtime lists) has the same machine code in both releases: of timeranger2.c only purge_key_files() changed (archive_purged_files() is inlined in it), and of helpers.c only build_path() (+52 instructions), the date reader and two functions no append runs. In a run of the benchmark (360,000 appends) build_path() is called 82 times, at the opens, and the date reader never; the object of the benchmark itself is identical. 3,003 of the 3,237 functions of the binary moved, most by 1,536 or 64 bytes; 21 changed their 64-byte alignment, none of them on the append path. Measured again: 7.29.2 and 7.29.3 alternated for 10 rounds, -1.82% (t = -2.3), inside its noise; in a rotation of five builds (10 rounds), -2.47% (t = -3.6). The 7.29.3 binary relinked with all the libraries of 7.29.2 measures as 7.29.2 (+0.94%); relinked with only the gobj-c of 7.29.2, +0.57%; with only its timeranger2, -1.52%.
